title: Conflict and migration

draft.title: Conflict and migration
card: Conflict is armed fighting within or between countries. Forced migration is when people must leave their homes to stay safe, such as refugees who cross a border and people displaced inside their own country.
War can destroy hospitals, clinics and supply lines, and health workers may be killed or flee. Vaccination and care for pregnancy and chronic illness can then stop or fall.
Fighting damages farms, markets and water supplies, so food and clean water become scarce. Malnutrition and disease can follow. Homes may also be destroyed, and people may shelter in crowded camps.
Displaced people can face violence, injury and trauma on their journey and in camps. Crowding and poor sanitation can help diseases such as cholera and measles spread.
draft.remember: Conflict and forced migration damage the services and basics people need for health, and can expose them to violence and disease.

a.q: Why can a war raise the risk of disease in a country, even among people far from the fighting?
opts: Health services and clean water supplies break down
People stop moving, so diseases stay in one place
Fewer people are born, so there is less to treat
Soldiers carry diseases that civilians cannot catch
a.why: War can destroy clinics, supply lines and water systems, so prevention and treatment fall away. Disease does not depend on distance from the fighting. People can be far from it and still lose care and clean water.
a.clue: Think about what services and supplies a war can damage.

b.q: Thousands of people flee a war and settle in a crowded camp with few toilets. Which outcome is most directly linked to the camp conditions?
opts: Faster spread of infectious diseases such as cholera
Better access to long-term care for chronic illness
Lower risk of malnutrition as food is shared
Fewer injuries because people are away from the fighting
b.why: Crowding and poor sanitation help infectious diseases such as cholera spread quickly. Leaving the fighting may cut some injuries, but injury and trauma can still occur on the journey and in camps. This is not the outcome linked to the camp conditions.
b.clue: Consider what crowding and few toilets do to infections.

a.best: Health services and clean water supplies break down

b.best: Faster spread of infectious diseases such as cholera

problems.detail: The clue ('what services and supplies a war can damage') echoes the right option's wording ('Health services and clean water supplies'), so a student can match words without knowing the idea.
The clue ('what crowding and few toilets do to infections') names infections, which points straight to the only option about infectious disease and gives the answer away.
The why says 'Disease does not depend on distance from the fighting.' This is too absolute: risk is often higher near fighting. Better: 'People far from the fighting can still be at risk.'

check.summary: The card and answers are accurate, but both clues all but give the answers away by echoing the right option's wording. Why (a) also overstates that disease does not depend on distance from the fighting.
